concerns.text: The Local Non‑Additivity Index (LNAI) is defined as the point‑biserial correlation between (RF_error − Baseline_error) and the binary co‑presence of a fingerprint bit‑pair. Because the RF predictions (and thus the residuals) are themselves functions of the same fingerprint bits used as predictors, the outcome variable is not independent of the predictor set. This creates a circular/tautological validation: any systematic pattern in the residuals can be trivially linked to the bits that generated the predictions, inflating apparent significance of ‘non‑additivity’ zones. Without an external, independent validation (e.g., a held‑out dataset not used for model training or a different descriptor set), the LNAI cannot be interpreted as evidence of true non‑additive chemical interactions.
